title: DepoAudio export manifest, version 1
description: Written by DepoAudio as <output>.depoaudio.json next to each converted file. It records what was converted, by which build, and how. It never contains folder paths. Mirror of src-tauri/src/manifest.rs; a Rust test checks real manifests against this file.

createdAt.description: UTC time the manifest was written (RFC 3339, seconds).

fileName.description: File name only, never a folder path.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the original file as selected, before any format preparation.

trmInspectionError.description: Only for an FTR recording DepoAudio could not read, or in which it found no complete round of frames to split: why. FFmpeg's native ftr decoder then read the file as it is (ffmpeg -c:a ftr -i <source>), without DepoAudio's layout checks, and there is no trm object. Written by versions after 1.1.0.

trm.description: Only for an FTR recording (.trm, .ftr, .tll): what DepoAudio found when it read the file, and how FFmpeg decoded it. The layout reading follows the owner's interoperability notes and has been checked against a sample made by the owner's rebuild tool, not against a recording made by FTR. The USER (user name) and UDAT (free text) chunks are never copied here: only whether they hold text; the FILE chunk's text only when it is a name in the recorder's own format. Written by versions after 1.1.0.

tag.description: WAVEFORMATEX format tag as stored. Low 12 bits 0x180: FTR AAC; bit 0x4000: one mono stream per microphone; bit 0x8000: stereo streams.

audioCodec.description: The codec the tag's low 12 bits name. mp2, mp3 and wma are read by FFmpeg as ordinary audio (decodePath ffmpeg-plain). Written by versions after 1.1.0 that record it.

streamLayout.description: For FTR AAC, how the microphones are interleaved: one mono stream each (tag bit 0x4000) or stereo streams of two microphones (tag bit 0x8000); null for other codecs. Written by versions after 1.1.0 that record it.

channels.description: Channel (microphone) count from the audio format header.

streams.description: Interleaved AAC streams: channels for mono streams, channels / 2 for stereo streams; 0 for other codecs. Stream k of a stereo-stream file holds channels 2k and 2k + 1. Written by versions after 1.1.0 that record it.

channelsPerStream.description: 1 for mono streams, 2 for stereo streams; 0 for other codecs. Written by versions after 1.1.0 that record it.

sampleRate.description: From the first stream-0 AAC frame header; null when no frame was read (always for other codecs).

formatSampleRate.description: nSamplesPerSec of the audio format header. Written by versions after 1.1.0 that record it.

headerScale.description: Audio stream header dwScale as stored (1024 for FTR AAC). Written by versions after 1.1.0 that record it.

headerRate.description: Audio stream header dwRate as stored (the sample rate for FTR AAC). Written by versions after 1.1.0 that record it.

headerChunkCount.description: Audio stream header dwLength: the number of audio chunks the recorder counted when it closed the file. Null while it holds 0x7FFFFFFF (openEnded). Informational: packets is what was read. Written by versions after 1.1.0 that record it.

declaredStreams.description: Main header dwStreams as stored. It can count an input that has no stream header list (the level meter), so streamLists is what DepoAudio uses. Written by versions after 1.1.0 that record it.

streamLists.description: strl lists present in the header. Written by versions after 1.1.0 that record it.

startBoundary.description: Main header flag 0x20000000: FTR joins no earlier file to this one.

endBoundary.description: Main header flag 0x40000000: FTR joins no later file to this one.

startUtc.description: The TUTC chunk (the file's start, UTC) as an RFC 3339 time ending in Z; null without the chunk. Written by versions after 1.1.0 that record it.

startLocal.description: The TLOC chunk (the same start in the recorder's local time) as a date and time with no offset; null without the chunk. Written by versions after 1.1.0 that record it.

startBasis.description: Which time gives startTime: TLOC (local, as a BWF time reference counts it), else TUTC (UTC), else the FILETIME in the FILE chunk's name (its time zone not stated); null when none is present. Written by versions after 1.1.0 that record it.

recordedFileName.description: The FILE chunk: the name the recorder gave this file, only when it is in the recorder's own name format (see recordedFileNamePresent); null otherwise. Written by versions after 1.1.0 that record it.

recordedFileNamePresent.description: The FILE chunk holds text. Its text is recorded in recordedFileName only when it is a file name in the recorder's own format (name part of at most 28 letters, digits or !$`() +,-.=[]^'{}, then _YYYYMMDD-HHMM_ and the FILETIME as 16 lowercase hex digits matching that date and time, then an extension); any other text is never recorded. Written by versions after 1.1.0 that record it.

userNamePresent.description: A USER chunk holds a user name. The name itself is never recorded. Written by versions after 1.1.0 that record it.

userDataPresent.description: A UDAT chunk holds free text. The text itself is never recorded. Written by versions after 1.1.0 that record it.

signature.description: SIGN/CERT chunks follow the index. DepoAudio does not check (or write) signatures. Written by versions after 1.1.0 that record it.

openEnded.description: The audio length field holds the value a recorder leaves in a file it never closed; the duration then comes from the frames read.

indexKind.description: How the audio chunks were found: the idx1 index (absolute or movi-relative offsets) or a walk of the movi list; not-read when the codec is not FTR AAC and FFmpeg read the file as it is.

frames.description: AAC frames delivered to the channels (whole rounds only).

straddlingFrames.description: Frames that begin in one audio chunk and end in a later one.

misalignedPackets.description: Audio chunks that do not start and end on a channel-0 round boundary.

multiRoundPackets.description: Audio chunks that hold more than one whole round of frames. Written by versions after 1.1.0 that check it.

resyncSkippedBytes.description: Bytes skipped before the first channel-0 frame.

channelResyncs.description: Times the channel order broke after the first channel-0 frame (a channel-0 frame where another channel's was due, or the reverse, as after a lost or extra frame): the partial round was dropped and dealing restarted at the next channel-0 frame. The round delivered just before a restart can hold a frame in the wrong slot. Written by versions after 1.1.0 that check it.

midStreamSkippedBytes.description: Unreadable bytes skipped after the first channel-0 frame and before the last frame delivered. Written by versions after 1.1.0 that check it.

paddingBytes.description: Zero bytes skipped between whole rounds or after the last one. Not treated as truncation. Written by versions after 1.1.0 that check it.

trailingSkippedBytes.description: Non-zero bytes after the last frame delivered that are not a frame. Written by versions after 1.1.0 that check it.

incompleteFinalRound.description: The last round was missing channels and was not delivered.

droppedFrames.description: Frames read but not delivered: their round was incomplete, or they were out of channel order.

droppedRounds.description: Incomplete rounds of frames dropped mid-recording (their frames were not delivered). The rounds the frames show to be missing are filled with silence (silenceFilled). Written by versions after 1.1.0 that check it.

silenceFilled.description: Where DepoAudio put silence in every channel in place of rounds of frames missing mid-recording, so that later audio keeps its time from the start, in order. When the channel order breaks, the fill is the fewest whole rounds (1024 samples each) that hold the frames seen between two channel-0 frames, less the round delivered: that is right when frames went missing and none were added. Frames missing in a run as long as a whole round (one per stream) leave frames that still look like whole rounds, so such a loss leaves no trace and is not filled; a repeated frame looks like a lost one and is filled. The silence is an AAC frame with an empty spectrum, so the decoder still fades the frame before it out across the stretch, and the frame after it fades in. Nothing is put in after the last round delivered. At most 1000 places are listed; silenceFilledGaps counts them all. Written by versions after 1.1.0 that fill.

atSample.description: Where the silence starts, in samples from the first frame delivered, at sampleRate (silence put in earlier counts).

samples.description: Samples of silence each channel got: whole rounds of 1024.

channels.description: Channels that got it: every channel of the recording.

reason.description: missing-frames: the channel order broke there, so frames are missing. unreadable-data: unreadable data was skipped there too; how much audio it held is not known, so later audio may still be earlier than its time from the start (startTime.note says so).

silenceFilledGaps.description: Places filled with silence, listed in silenceFilled or not. Written by versions after 1.1.0 that fill.

silenceFilledSamples.description: Samples of silence put in each channel, in all; durationSecs counts them. Written by versions after 1.1.0 that fill.

walkGaps.description: Places where the walk of the movi list met data that is not a chunk (an unreadable chunk header, a zero gap, a chunk size past the end) and looked ahead for the next audio chunk. Written by versions after 1.1.0 that check it.

walkGapBytes.description: Bytes the walk skipped at those places (0 for a chunk written without its pad byte). The audio they held is missing and its length is not known. Written by versions after 1.1.0 that check it.

indexMismatch.description: idx1 does not list every audio chunk: movi holds audio chunks after the last one listed, or the number listed is not the header's chunk count (headerChunkCount, ftra.d). The chunks were then found by walking movi when that found more. Written by versions after 1.1.0 that check it.

lengthHighBitFrames.description: Delivered frames with either of the two ADTS frame-length bits FTR ignores set; DepoAudio cleared them in the temporary channel files. Written by versions after 1.1.0 that check it.

frameChannelMismatches.description: Delivered frames whose ADTS channel configuration is not channelsPerStream. A file with any is not split. Written by versions after 1.1.0 that check it.

truncated.description: The file ends inside a chunk or a frame, or its chunk list stops at unreadable data.

continuationSegments.description: RIFF AVIX (OpenDML) segments after the first RIFF. DepoAudio does not read their audio: the counts cover the first segment only and durationSecs is null. Written by versions after 1.1.0 that check it.

grewWhileRead.description: The file grew between DepoAudio's inspection and its channel split (a recording still being written); only the part inspected was converted. Written by versions after 1.1.0 that check it.

ftra.description: The optional FTRA chunk's five values, as read; null when the file has none. Reported only; DepoAudio does not use them.

videoStreams.description: Video stream headers in the file; video is never converted.

durationSecs.description: (Frames per channel + rounds filled with silence) x 1024 samples / sample rate; null when no frame was found or the file has continuation segments.

decodePath.description: native-ftr: FFmpeg's ftr decoder read the file as it is. deinterleaved: DepoAudio wrote each stream to a temporary ADTS file (mono, or stereo for stereo streams; descrambled, equal frame counts) and FFmpeg joined them in channel order with amerge. ffmpeg-plain: MP2, MP3 or WMA audio, read by FFmpeg as it is with the decoder it picks.

routeReasons.description: Why the native decoder was not used; empty for native-ftr.

inputOptions.description: The options FFmpeg was given before each -i: ["-c:a", "ftr"] before the recording itself (native-ftr), ["-f", "aac"] before each temporary channel file (deinterleaved), or none (ffmpeg-plain). Written by versions after 1.1.0 that record it.

inputCount.description: How many -i inputs FFmpeg read: 1 for native-ftr and ffmpeg-plain, or one temporary file per stream for deinterleaved, which filterChain joins in channel order with amerge before anything else. The temporary files are deleted afterwards. Written by versions after 1.1.0 that record it.

dmTimeline.description: Only for a DigitalCAT / SoundSync .dm source, whose audio DepoAudio reads into a temporary WAV before FFmpeg decodes it. Lists the blocks read, the recorded-over blocks that were skipped, what was left out after a short block or an incomplete block, where the block time stamps jump, and counts from a .bmf marker file beside the .dm. Blocks are read in file order up to the first short block or incomplete block, which is where the format notes say SoundSync's player stops. Stamps are whole seconds (UTC), so they place a block to within about a second; the notes say a recording stamps about the end of each block and a WAV import the start, and the file does not say which made it. Positions come from block counts, not stamps. Nothing here is written into the output audio. Written by versions after 1.1.0; absent for every other source.

formatTag.description: The WAVEFORMATEX wFormatTag stored in the .dm (0x0031, 49, is GSM 6.10).

codecName.description: The FFmpeg decoder DepoAudio expects for formatTag (for example gsm_ms or pcm_s16le), or the tag in hex when it has no name for it.

blockSize.description: Block size in bytes from the .dm header.

blocksTotal.description: Blocks read: complete blocks in file order, up to and including the first short block. An incomplete block at the end (truncatedTailBytes) and anything after a short block (bytesAfterShortBlock) are not counted.

blocksErased.description: Blocks whose stamp is 0 (recorded over). Their audio is stale and was left out.

shortFinalBlock.description: The last block read is shorter than blockSize and its whole codec blocks are kept, with a warning: the format notes say SoundSync's own player does not play a short block. False when that short block was recorded over (stamp 0): it is then counted in blocksErased only, and none of it is used.

lastBlockBytesDropped.description: Bytes at the end of a kept short last block that were less than one whole codec block and were left out.

bytesAfterShortBlock.description: Bytes of the file after a short block that is not at the end of the file. The format notes say SoundSync's player stops at a short block, and SoundSync finds blocks (including the ones it marks as recorded over) by their fixed spacing, which a short block breaks; so these bytes were not read as blocks and are not in the audio. warnings names the short block.

truncatedTailBytes.description: Bytes at the end of the file after the last complete block: a block the file ends partway through (for example a recording or copy that did not finish). They were left out of the audio.

stampsMonotonic.description: False when a later block has an earlier stamp than the block before it. Only that is observed, not the cause; the file does not say why. A recorder clock set back during the session would do it. Recorded-over blocks (stamp 0) are skipped in this comparison, and the layout notes say a record-over appends its new blocks with later stamps, so a record-over alone does not set this false.

segments.description: Runs of kept blocks, in file order. A new segment starts where a stamp moves forward by more than 2 seconds (a pause) or moves backwards.

startSample.description: First sample of the segment in the decoded source audio, at the source's sample rate and before any trim or resampling. Null when the codec's samples per block are not known.

firstStampUtc.description: The stamp of the segment's first block as stored, in UTC (1 second resolution). Not adjusted: for a recording the notes say it marks about the end of that block, for a WAV import its start.

segmentsOmitted.description: Segments after the first 1000, counted but not listed.

warnings.description: Facts that did not stop the conversion, such as a block size other than the one this audio format usually gets, a short block (kept, but not played by SoundSync), what was left out after a short block, or an incomplete block at the end.

markerFile.description: A SoundSync bookmark file (.bmf) beside the .dm, found by SoundSync's naming rule (the .dm's name with .bmf for the extension, letter case ignored). Only read, and only counted: marker text is never recorded. Absent when there is no such file.

status.description: read: its FileInfo stream was read. unreadable: see problem. ambiguous: several files have the name in different letter case and none is the all lower-case name SoundSync writes, so none was read.

sizeBytes.description: The marker file's size. No hash of it is recorded: the file is mostly its marker text, so a hash would let a reader confirm a guess at that text. Null when the name is a link, which is not followed.

entries.description: Bookmark entries in the FileInfo stream.

entriesWithText.description: Entries that carry text. The text itself is not recorded.

entriesInSoundsyncRange.description: Entries SoundSync would keep on opening the file: positions from 0 to its timeline length (the sound bytes its loader counts divided by the byte rate, in whole seconds, times 1000 ms).

entriesMatchingABlock.description: Kept entries whose clock time (first block's stamp plus the position in whole seconds, as SoundSync seeks) is the stamp of a block DepoAudio read. The others point into a pause, at a recorded-over stretch, or past what was read.

problem.description: Why the file could not be read, in DepoAudio's words; never any of its content.

fileName.description: File name only; the manifest sits next to this file.

wavHeader.description: For a WAV output, the header read from the file's first four bytes after encoding: riff (plain RIFF) or rf64 (written once a file passes the 4 GiB RIFF limit). Null for other formats. Written by versions after 1.1.0.

filterOption.description: The FFmpeg option that carried filterChain, or null when no filter ran.

filterChain.description: The exact FFmpeg filter string used. In split mode it is the whole graph; channel.sourceChannelIndex names this file's branch.

encoderArgs.description: The exact FFmpeg encoder and metadata arguments for this output, without file paths. Stream selection is in mapArgs.

mapArgs.description: The exact FFmpeg -map arguments for this output: for stereo and keep, -map 0:a:0 (the converted source stream), or -map [da_out] when an FTR recording was read as one input per channel (filterChain then ends in [da_out]); -map [opN] (this channel's branch of filterChain) for split. The command is: ffmpeg <inputs> [filterOption filterChain] mapArgs encoderArgs <output>, where <inputs> is -i <source>, or for an FTR recording source.trm.inputCount times source.trm.inputOptions -i <input> (the recording itself, or each temporary channel file in channel order). Written by versions after 1.1.0.

fadeOut.description: Where the fade-out (afade=t=out in filterChain) was placed, or null when there is none. It is placed from decodedSourceSeconds, the converted stream's length as FFmpeg decodes it, not from statedSourceSeconds, the length the source's headers state, which can be shorter (a chained Ogg file, a VBR MP3). Written by versions after 1.1.0.

sourceChannelIndex.description: Zero-based source channel for a split file (FFmpeg c0 is 0); null otherwise.

label.description: The channel or microphone label the person entered for this split file.

labels.description: Labels entered for each source channel, in channel order.

audioStream.description: Which audio stream of the source was converted. Written by versions after 1.1.0; records written by 1.1.0 do not have it. Every probe and FFmpeg pass maps this one stream explicitly (-map 0:a:<index>), so the channel facts above describe it.

index.description: Zero-based index among the source's audio streams (FFmpeg a:0 is 0).

sourceAudioStreamCount.description: How many audio streams the source has, or null when the probe could not read them.

source.description: bwf-bext-time-reference: the source's own bext chunk. ftr-tloc, ftr-tutc, ftr-file-name: an FTR recording's TLOC (local) or TUTC (UTC) chunk, or the FILETIME in its FILE chunk's name (time zone not stated); see source.trm.startBasis. The ftr values are written by versions after 1.1.0.

sourceTimeReferenceSamples.description: BWF bext TimeReference of the source, or for an FTR recording the time of day of its start: samples since midnight at sourceSampleRate.

outputTimeReferenceSamples.description: The same start, rescaled to output.sampleRate. Null when the output start differs from the source start (leading-silence trim) or the start is unknown.

writtenToOutput.description: True when the output WAV carries outputTimeReferenceSamples in its own bext chunk. When false, the output carries no time_reference at all and this record is the only place the start is kept. A start that is not local time of day (ftr-tutc, ftr-file-name) is never written to an output, since a bext time reference counts from local midnight.
